scope: R210: a standalone measurement refutes the R209 hypothesis that HCCL all-reduce reduction order is non-deterministic

evidence: libhccl.so contains: HCCL_DETERMINISTIC set by default to [false]
libhccl.so contains: ErrToWarn: HCCL_DETERMINISTIC is set to [%s], which is incorrect

design.input: identical on every rank via manual_seed(1234+n)
design.comparison: sha256 of the result buffer after clone plus barrier
design.config_tested: HCCL_DETERMINISTIC unset, i.e. the default false

verdict: all-reduce is bit-reproducible by default, so HCCL_DETERMINISTIC is not even needed; the R209 hypothesis is refuted
consequence: the non-determinism must be operator level rather than collective level

narrowed_candidates.candidate: matmul tiling or split-K accumulation order
narrowed_candidates.how_to_test: repeat a single matmul operator on identical input and compare bits

narrowed_candidates.candidate: reduction order inside the FA TIK kernel

next_step: a single-operator bit-repeat probe over matmul, FA and norm, which is far cheaper than running the whole model and needs no weights at all
value: eliminated a whole class of candidates, narrowing issue 15s search space
showed this kind of hypothesis is testable without the model, cutting the cost from about 16 minutes to about 1
produced a reusable probe structure for operator-level tests
for issue 4: if the operators themselves prove bit-reproducible then prefetch safety concerns correctness rather than numeric jitter, which makes 4 simpler
limits: the input was identical across ranks, whereas the real model has different per-rank values; the reduction path would differ numerically although the randomness hypothesis is already excluded
only HCCL_DETERMINISTIC unset was run, since it was already reproducible and =1 adds no information
only all-reduce was tested, not reduce-scatter or all-gather
